GNU Wget can download a file, a folder or a whole website, but only if you remember which of its many switches to combine. **Fetch** lets you build the command visually instead. It covers every option in `wget --help` for version 1.21 (155 settings), explains what each one does, and warns about risky choices. It runs entirely in your browser; nothing is uploaded.

Fetch started as a Wget companion to my Robocopy tool and was redesigned as part of **Conduit**, a pair of command builders that share one design system. Its sister app is [Mirror](../robocopy-gui/index.qmd), the Robocopy builder.

## How it works

1. **Pick a starting point.** Choose a preset (One file, Offline site copy, Images only, Check for broken links, or Gentle crawl) or start from scratch.
2. **Fill in the tabs.** Target, What to download, Save layout, Filters, Performance, Requests, Security, Logging and Advanced. Rarely used options stay hidden until you turn on **Show advanced**.
3. **Watch the command.** It updates as you choose, with every flag explained and notes for risky choices such as skipping certificate checks, putting a password in the command, or crawling with no wait.
4. **Add to queue.** Build several downloads, reorder them, then download one `.bat` or `.ps1` script. Stop on first failure is on by default.

## Other ways in

- **Find an option.** Type a name or a flag, such as `cookies` or `--limit-rate`, to search every tab at once.
- **Paste a command.** Paste an existing `wget` command and the form fills in. Flags the builder does not recognise are kept under Advanced.
- **Command palette.** `Ctrl+K` jumps to any option, preset or page, and `Ctrl+Enter` adds the current command to the queue.
- **Profiles.** Save a full set of options and load it later. Profiles, the queue and the form are remembered in your browser.

## Technical details

Fetch is one self-contained `index.html` with no build step to run it and no backend, so your URLs and credentials never leave the browser. It is generated from the shared source in the [Mirror repository](https://github.com/ar-puuk/robocopy-gui), so the two apps keep identical design tokens and components. Icons are from [Lucide](https://lucide.dev) and the fonts are Bricolage Grotesque, Instrument Sans and JetBrains Mono. The code lives in the [source repository](https://github.com/ar-puuk/wget-gui).

## Use cases

- **Digital archivists** creating offline mirrors of websites before they go offline
- **Developers** checking a site for broken links
- **Bulk downloaders** working through long lists of files from a list file
- **Students** learning Wget syntax by seeing what each option does
